p: Anyone who recites an orphaned amen,
his children will be orphaned; … abbreviated … his days will be abbreviated … a truncated … his days will be truncated. … One who extends his amen,

his children will be orphaned; one who recites an abbreviated amen, his days will be abbreviated and incomplete; one who recites a truncated amen, his days will be truncated. One who extends his amen,
they will extend his days and years for him.

p: Rav’s students were seated at a meal … Rav Aḥa entered.
Rav’s students were seated at a meal when Rav Aḥa entered.
A great man has come who can recite the blessing on our behalf.
Do you think that the greatest recites the blessing? … the main … of the meal recites the blessing. … The halakha … is that the greatest … recites the blessing,

Do you think that the greatest recites the blessing? That is not so. Rather, one of the main participants who was present from the beginning of the meal recites the blessing. The Gemara concludes: The halakha, however, is that the greatest person present recites the blessing,
even if he arrived at the end
